meta.title: What is patent insurance? | Patent Insurance Strategy
meta.description: Definition, features and three patent insurance products proposed for Vietnam: application, legal expenses and infringement liability insurance.

header.title:
Transferring and spreading
patent risk
header.lead:
Insurers share the legal risk,
so inventors can innovate with confidence.

stages.label: Before grant
stages.body: The application is refused and costs are sunk.

stages.label: After grant
stages.body: The patent may face cancellation or invalidation.

stages.label: During use
stages.body: Sued for infringement, or infringed by others.

stages.label: After expiry
stages.body: Legal risk can persist after the right ends.

traits.title: A negative right
traits.body: A patent lets you exclude others; it does not guarantee your own freedom to operate.

traits.title: Can be invalidated
traits.body: Even after examination, a patent can be revoked at any time.

traits.title: Law meets technology
traits.body: Scope depends on how the claims are interpreted.

items.title: Non-life insurance
items.body: Created by contract, works like civil insurance.

items.title: Intangible subject
items.body: Intellectual assets are hard to quantify and price.

items.title: Focused on infringement
items.body: Both defending claims and enforcing your rights.

items.title: Financial support
items.body: Pays the cost of resolving disputes instead of restoring an asset, as traditional insurance does.

compare.note: Phase 1 launches the first two products at a basic level. Phase 2 adds no new product; it widens the coverage and protection of those same two products. Infringement liability insurance comes only in Phase 3.

items.q: Is patent risk too uncertain to insure?
items.a: Risk arises at well-defined procedural points and falls into five groups: intrinsic, environmental, innovation, licensing demands and NPEs. It can be identified and managed.
Insurers can use proxies such as dispute frequency, duration and average awards. Risk can also be split into layers and spread through reinsurance.
The State can subsidise early premiums, as Japan and China do. Tiered products let SMEs buy smaller cover. Premiums fall as market data builds up.
